summary: Surface Pro 9 accelerometer not initializing after SCCM image; rotation locked
description:
Issue summary: New Surface Pro 9 units provisioned through the corporate SCCM imaging pipeline arrive with screen rotation stuck in portrait and system reports no accelerometer device. Impact: Users cannot auto-rotate display or use orientation-aware apps. Repro rate: 6/12 devices in recent batch.
Initial reporter noticed after applying standard Windows 11 image with DriverCatalog v4. Steps and logs attached below.
steps_to_reproduce: Boot Surface Pro 9 from USB boot media running SCCM task sequence
Apply corporate Windows 11 22H2 image with default driver package 'Corp-Drivers-2026-02'
Complete autopilot/azuread join and install company apps
Reboot and check Device Manager > Sensors
Attempt to rotate screen using orientation setting and notify double-tap to trigger sensor
logs: System event 03-01T10:22:44: SensorCollectionService failed to enumerate sensors: 0x57
DriverInstaller 03-01T10:23:10: 'IMU_HID' driver install returned SUCCESS but no sensor presence
ACPI 03-01T10:23:12: BIOS reported sensor table absent (ACPI: SNC0 not found)
SCCM task sequence log smsts.log shows driver package applied from DP01 without errors
comments: 2026-03-01 11:00 - Noah Kim: Acknowledge. Collecting msinfo, Device Manager print and smsts logs from affected unit. Will try manual driver install.
2026-03-01 12:40 - Aisha Fernandez: Attached msinfo32 and smsts.log for two affected units. Both show 'Sensors' category empty.

2026-03-02 09:15 - Noah Kim: Manual install of Microsoft IMU/HID driver (from vendor bundle) briefly surfaces 'Inclinometer' but disappears after reboot. Suspect ACPI table exposure issue after BIOS v1.0.14.
2026-03-03 14:05 - SRE (Riley Chen): Saw similar reports on #endpoint-ops. Suggested test: imaging with latest BIOS v1.0.16 and driver package Corp-Drivers-2026-03.
2026-03-04 10:30 - Noah Kim: Imaging a test unit with BIOS 1.0.16 + updated driver package fixed sensor enumeration. Preparing remediation plan and hotfix task sequence.
2026-03-05 16:10 - Aisha Fernandez: Confirmed rotation works on 3 newly imaged devices after hotfix. Marking resolved and creating follow-up INT-18390 for image update rollout.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Recent BIOS firmware (1.0.14) on Surface Pro 9 does not expose ACPI sensor table required for IMU enumeration; later BIOS 1.0.16 restores table.
Reproduced on lab unit by imaging with 2026-02 driver package and BIOS 1.0.14; accelerometer missing in Device Manager > Sensors.
Manual driver install sequence: pnputil /add-driver <imu.inf> /install — driver shows, but ACPI table missing causes device to disappear after reboot.
Tested imaging with BIOS 1.0.16 + Corp-Drivers-2026-03: IMU and Inclinometer persist across reboots. No kernel errors in event log.

Checked SCCM DP and driver package manifest; Corp-Drivers-2026-02 did not include vendor firmware shim that coordinates with BIOS 1.0.16. Recommended to pin BIOS version in provisioning pipeline and include firmware shim in driver package.
resolution: Applied workaround: created SCCM hotfix task sequence that applies BIOS 1.0.16 followed by Corp-Drivers-2026-03 driver package. Deployed to affected batch (6 devices) and verified sensor enumeration and rotation on all. Root cause: regression introduced by earlier BIOS that hid ACPI sensor table; fix requires BIOS update and updated driver package. Follow-up actions: 1) Update golden image to include BIOS 1.0.16 and Corp-Drivers-2026-03 (see INT-18390). 2) Add sensor enumeration check to provisioning validation automation. 3) Notify procurement to avoid shipping units with 1.0.14 BIOS. Postmortem to be added to Confluence.
